title: Reproducing Hung 1987: fixed charge and trap density of thin oxides

sample.paper: “p-type (boron doped) Si wafers with (100) surface orientation and 15-22 ohm-cm resistivity”; Czochralski, 525 µm, 100 mm, quartered
Boron, 15-22 Ω·cm (chapters 4, 5) or 15-25 Ω·cm (Appendix specification); measured about 1×10^15 cm⁻³
sample.ours: DOPING: p_type_boron (recorded; no program reads it)

sample.paper: “a standard “RCA clean” … (g) etched in 5% HF/H2O at 25C for 10 sec” before every high-temperature step and metal deposition
8000 Å field oxide at 1050 °C (100 min); for chapter 4 also a phosphorus predeposition at 1000 °C and 60 min drive-in at 1050 °C
sample.note: The gate region is etched to bare silicon after these, so they do not reach the gate oxide, but they are 2 to 3 h at 1000-1050 °C on the same wafer.

sample.paper: Chapter 4: Al-gate n-MOSFETs 200 × 200 µm and capacitors, packaged in TO-5. Chapter 5: capacitors of 4×10^-4 cm², probed on the wafer, back contact not sintered
“Purest commercially available O2 and N2 with residual moisture <2 vpm”, further dried by traps
sample.ours: dry_O2 or mix:O2=…,N2=…; moisture not written
sample.note: 2 vpm could be written as H2O in the mix; no program reads it.

history.item: Field oxide, 8000 Å, dry-wet-dry at 1050 °C
history.ours: not in our history
history.note: Chapter 4 calls the cycle “wet-dry-wet” (PDF p. 122); chapter 5 and the Appendix “dry-wet-dry”. The gate windows are later etched to bare silicon, so the field oxide does not reach the gate oxide; its heat does reach the wafer.

history.item: Phosphorus source and drain: predeposition at 1000 °C, drive-in 60 min at 1050 °C in O2
history.paper: “(a) Predeposition … 1000C … (c) Drive-in O2 (1000 ml/min.) 1050C 60 min.”
history.ours: not in our history
history.note: Transistor wafers only; skipped for the capacitor-only wafers of chapter 5 (PDF p. 253).

history.item: Gate windows opened in buffered HF
history.paper: “immersed in buffered HF solution (HF:NH4F:H2O = 2:1:7 …) until the wafer surface not protected by photoresist becomes hydrophobic”
history.ours: not in our history

history.item: RCA clean ending in 10 s of 5% HF
history.paper: “Before every high temperature step and metal deposition, the wafers received a standard “RCA clean” … (g) etched in 5% HF/H2O at 25C for 10 sec.”
history.ours: CLEAN: peroxide_HF on the sample; no operator reads it
history.note: Chapter 5 words it as “a sequence of peroxide-based solutions, followed by a 5% HF/H2O dip”.

history.item: Boat-in, 3 min, in the oxidation gas
history.paper: “Boat-in: N2 (1200 ml/min.) + O2 (300 ml/min.) 1050C 3 min.”
history.ours: RUN BoatInCh4 DURATION 180 TEMP 1050->1050 AMBIENT mix:O2=0.2,N2=0.8
history.note: Not in the datasets' recipe. Written at the furnace temperature; the wafer heats during it. The range runs from almost nothing (the 3 min counted inside the Table 4.1 time) to 3 min added to it.

history.item: Gate oxidation, 1050 °C, 20% O2 in N2, 8 min
history.paper: “grown at 1050C in an ambient of diluted dry oxygen in nitrogen (20% O2 by volume)”; time from Table 4.1a
history.ours: RUN Oxidation DURATION 480 TEMP 1050->1050 AMBIENT mix:O2=0.2,N2=0.8
history.note: Gases “<2 vpm” moisture, further dried by traps (Appendix A); no HCl.

history.item: In-situ nitrogen anneal, 1050 °C, 30 min
history.paper: “Anneal: N2 (1000 ml/min.) 1050C 30 min.”; “followed by in-situ post-oxidation-annealing (POA) in nitrogen at 1050C for 30 minutes”
history.ours: RUN NitrogenAnneal DURATION 1800 TEMP 1050->1050 AMBIENT inert_N2

history.item: Boat-out, 3 min, in nitrogen
history.paper: “Boat-out: N2 (1000 ml/min.) 1050C 3 min.”
history.ours: RUN BoatOut DURATION 180 TEMP 1050->400 AMBIENT inert_N2
history.note: Not in the datasets' recipe. The time is the Appendix's; the temperature path is ours: a straight fall to 400 °C.

history.item: Source and drain contact windows opened
history.paper: “After gate-oxidation, windows were opened for the source and drain contacts.”
history.ours: not in our history

history.item: Pure aluminium, 1 µm, from a tungsten filament
history.paper: “A layer of pure aluminium, of about 1 um thick, was then deposited … in a pressure below 10^-5 Torr … which employed a tungsten filament … The wafers were kept cool by using a heat sink”
history.ours: not in our history

history.item: Nitrogen flush at 400 °C before the anneal, 15 min
history.paper: “N2(1000 ml/min.) 400C 15 min.” … “The flushing with N2 during initial and final stages of annealing is merely a safety precaution”
history.ours: RUN PMAFlushIn DURATION 900 TEMP 400->400 AMBIENT inert_N2
history.note: General Appendix recipe; chapter 4 does not repeat it.

history.item: Forming gas, 400 °C, 30 min
history.paper: “To inactivate the interface traps, all the samples were further annealed in forming gas (10% H2 + 90% N2) at 400C for 30 min.”
history.ours: RUN PostMetalAnneal DURATION 1800 TEMP 400->400 AMBIENT forming_gas_H2
history.note: Not in the datasets' recipe. The fixed-charge program drops hydrogen steps; the trap-density program reads it.

history.item: Nitrogen flush at 400 °C after the anneal, 15 min
history.ours: RUN PMAFlushOut DURATION 900 TEMP 400->400 AMBIENT inert_N2

history.item: Lapped to 150 µm, scribed, bonded, sealed in TO-5
history.paper: “the wafers were lapped down to a thickness of 150 um, then scribed, bonded, and sealed in multilead TO-5 packages”
history.ours: not in our history

history.item: 1 MHz and quasi-static C-V; thickness from the 10 Hz accumulation capacitance
history.paper: “(eps_ox/d_ox)(phi_MS - V_FB) = Qf + Qit(0)”; “The Al-Si workfunction difference was found to be -0.715 +/- 0.005V”; “The gate oxide thickness is extracted from the accumulation capacitance measured at 10Hz.”
history.ours: the observables Nf, Dit and Thickness
history.note: φMS was taken from the zero-thickness intercept of the etched-back capacitors, so Qf depends on the etched-back series being right.

history.item: Chapter 5 withdrawal
history.paper: “pulled out from the central zone of furnace under the oxidation ambient in less than 3 sec”
history.ours: RUN Pull DURATION 3 TEMP T->400 in the oxidation gas
history.note: Not in the stored recipes; the library records it on the source.

history.item: Chapter 5 boat-in
history.paper: “Boat-in: O2 (1500 ml/min.) 900C 3 min.”
history.ours: RUN BoatInCh5 DURATION 180, VARY duration 1..180

history.item: Anneal series withdrawal
history.paper: not stated
history.ours: RUN PullAfterAnneal DURATION 180 in N2, VARY duration 3..180 and T_end

history.item: Anneal series oxidation time
history.ours: 20 min here; the datasets store 27 min

history.item: Chapter 5 forming gas
history.paper: one half of each wafer, 400 °C, 10 min
history.ours: the halves compared here are the unannealed ones; event Cleave

history.item: Chapter 5 etched-back control (Figure 5.5)
history.paper: four oxides grown together at 900 °C to about 350 Å, etched in dilute HF to 128-327 Å
history.ours: not reproduced: no trap density is printed for them, only a figure

steps.name: PullAfterAnneal
steps.label: Withdrawal after the anneal, in nitrogen (not described)
steps.isl: RUN PullAfterAnneal DURATION 180 TEMP 900->400 AMBIENT inert_N2
steps.paper: not stated: the fast pull is described only for the end of an oxidation
steps.timing: Neither the time, the gas nor the cooling is given

steps.name: Metal
steps.label: Pure aluminium, 1 µm, from a tungsten filament, onto unheated wafers
steps.paper: “A layer of pure aluminium, of about 1 um thick, was then deposited … tungsten filament … The wafers were kept cool”

steps.name: BackContact
steps.label: Back oxide swabbed off in dilute HF, thick aluminium on the back, not sintered
steps.paper: “the oxide layer on backside of wafer was stripped-off with dilute HF using a swab, followed by deposition of a thick Al film. The metal-silicon contacts were not sintered”

steps.name: Cleave
steps.label: Wafer split in two; one half to forming gas, 400 °C, 10 min
steps.paper: “Finally, each wafer was split into two halves and one of them was annealed in forming gas (10% H2 in N2) at 400C for 10 min.”

steps.name: NoAnneal
steps.label: No post-metallization anneal (this half)
steps.paper: the half not annealed: the trap densities of Figures 5.4 and 5.9 are this half's

steps.name: CV
steps.label: 1 MHz and quasi-static C-V on the probe station, in dry nitrogen
steps.paper: “The wafers were tested under a dry nitrogen atmosphere in a lightproof and screened probe station.”; thickness “measured by C-V method (assumes dielectric constant of SiO2 = 3.9)”
